analysis:
Documentation-only changes in docs/provider/cli-reference.md and docs/provider/troubleshooting.md. The cli-reference patch adds a `Requests served since the daemon started` status description (head lines 1020-1031). The head excerpts I received (lines 1300-2017) show only unchanged surrounding material, including env passthrough, SSD cache, token path, fan helper and App Attest worker documentation. troubleshooting.md bumps the date and rewords the `usage reporting` doctor row (line 87). It also adds a row at head line 144 explaining that `Requests served` can differ from console Earnings. This is an operator-facing counter explanation, not a trust or billing control.

No code, auth, attestation, encryption, cache-storage or authorization behavior is altered, and no secrets or new endpoints are introduced. The new text links to an immutable platform heartbeat.go revision (10b8b4fa...) and to source files I have not seen. I cannot verify the claims about coordinator payment for cancelled requests, `cumulativeDelta`, or the accuracy of the cited source. This is a documentation-accuracy matter, not a security regression.

The revised `usage reporting` row now says `usageGaps` counts completed requests with a missing usage chunk. That is a semantic change to a diagnostic, and billing-relevant behavior (A-009) lives in the platform. The doc change itself does not alter billing or threat assumptions; it only clarifies that `Requests served` is not a paid-jobs count.

Threat-model relevance: T-007/T-008 and TB-002 are unaffected. The retained T-041/SEC-035 cache text in the canonical model is not changed by this PR; the cache/SSD docs in the excerpt are unchanged context. One remaining question for integration is whether the `usageGaps` redefinition matches the code, which was not supplied.
